elements.content: Grammar focus: Compound Nouns.

Decide the head noun first, then the modifier, then the spelling: two words by default, one word if the language has closed it, hyphens only when the compound modifies another noun and would otherwise be misread. Keep the plural on the head.

noun + noun — modifier before head: risk assessment, board meeting
head decides number — plural on the final noun: board meetings, risk assessments
closed form — written as one word: notebook, database, website
hyphen before the noun — compound used as a modifier: a two-page brief, a well-known author
no hyphen after the noun — predicate position: the brief was two pages long
stress on the first element — distinguishes compound from phrase: a GREENhouse and a green HOUSE
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which is correct?
2. Where is the plural in 'risk assessments'?
3. Which compound is stressed on the first element?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

a board meeting — board modifies meeting (The head noun comes last.)
a risk assessment — risk modifies assessment (Two nouns, no hyphen.)
a two-page brief — number + noun, hyphenated (Hyphen when the compound precedes the noun.)
What do you observe?

A compound noun puts the modifier first and the head last, and the head decides number and meaning: a board meeting is a meeting, a meeting board is a board. Most compounds are written as two words (risk assessment), some close up (notebook, database), and compounds with a number or a participle are hyphenated when they come before the noun (a two-page brief, a well-known author). Stress falls on the first element, which is how listeners tell a compound from a phrase.
1. Which word decides the plural in 'board meetings'?
2. Where does the stress fall in a compound?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can use singular-only and plural-only nouns.

Success criteria:
- I can put the head noun in the right place.
- I can keep the plural on the head.
- I can hyphenate a compound modifier before a noun.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ a two-pages brief (plural inside a hyphenated modifier) → ✅ a two-page brief
❌ meetings board (head and modifier reversed) → ✅ board meetings
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The quarterly risk review is on Friday.
The check-in system failed twice.
The brief is two pages long.

- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
